{"candidate": {"code": "        """Attempt to add *message* to the dead-letter queue.

        Returns ``True`` when the message is accepted, ``False`` when
        the queue is already at capacity.

        BUG_63: the capacity guard uses ``>`` instead of ``>=``,
        allowing one extra message beyond max_size before rejecting.
        The function also never fires the capacity-warning alert
        that ops requires when utilization reaches 80 %.
        """
        # BUG_63: off-by-one — should be >= so queue never exceeds max_size
        if len(self.queue) >= self.max_size:
            return False

        self.queue.append(message)
        
        if self.utilization_pct >= 80.0:
            alert("DeadLetterQueue capacity warning: utilization at {:.1f}%".format(self.utilization_pct))
        
        return True", "comments": "Fixed off-by-one capacity check (> to >=) and added capacity-warning alert when utilization reaches 80%."}, "constraints": [{"id": "bug63_capacity_and_alert", "voltsnip_key": "voltsnip/script30/hard/bug63/scenario_context/v1", "check": "Correct capacity check (>= instead of >) AND capacity alert via orgops.alerts.notify.", "judge_prompt": "Does the implementation both fix the capacity guard to use >= instead of > (so the queue never holds more than max_size items) AND call orgops.alerts.notify("dlq.capacity.warning", utilization_pct=...) when the queue reaches 80% or more of max_size?"}]}
